description.narrative: Girls and young women (age 14 till 24) are the primary target group of the She Leads programme. Especially those that experience intersecting forms of discrimination and exclusion such as GYW living in poor, remot rural areas and urban slums, GYW experiencing GBV, GYW with different abilities, GYW who are out of school, GYW from sexual minority groups and refugees and internally displaced GYW. In addition, the programme works closely with CSO organisations and networks, (representatives of) formal institutions and community members and leaders.

In all She Leads countries, girls and young women, particularly GYW from socially excluded and exploited groups, are denied the opportunity to voice their interests and to participate meaningfully in decision-making processes. While many countries have made impressive strides in, for example, GYW’s access to education and the introduction of new laws against GBV, their socio-political participation continues to be much lower than that of boys and young men. Within the population of girls and young women (between age 14 till 24 years of age), there are specific groups of GYW in She Leads countries who suffer most from (intersectional) discrimination and exclusion.She Leads is a joint programme of Plan International Netherlands, Defence for Children - ECPAT the Netherlands (DCI-ECPAT), African Women’s Development and Communication Network (FEMNET), and Terre des Hommes the Netherlands (TdH). Equal Measures 2030 is a technical partner. The She Leads consortium brings together child rights organisations, feminist/women’s rights organisations, and GYW-led groups and aims to increase sustained influence of girls and young women (GYW) on decision-making and the transformation of gender norms in formal and informal institutions.

The long-term aim (impact) of She Leads is that GYW’s perspectives are included in gender responsive laws and policies and societal norms and practices. The strategic objective is to increase the sustained influence of GYW on decision-making and the transformation of gender norms in formal and informal institutions.Central to the She Leads programme is the enhancement of collective action of girls and young women in a gender-responsive civil society (civil society domain), support by increased acceptance of positive social gender norms (socio-cultural domain) and by enabling meaningful participation of girls and young women in decision-making by political institutions (institutional domain).

In the framework of capacity building strengthening, DCI lebanon planned a training on Gender Responsive Evaluation to generate and use evidence to enhance our organizational work to achieve gender equality&equity and women's empowerment. DCI conducted an advisory session with gender specialist and PMEAL specialist representative from a CSO to update DCI's internal complain/feedback mechanism, while incorporating GYW points of views and suggestions for this update.
Both our partners in Lebanon, Dar al Amal and DCI-Lebanon, are planning on building their own organisational capacity to enable better L&A on WRGE.

Our partner Dar al Amal was involved in the advocacy by starting an advocacy campaign on all social media (Facebook, Instagram). DAA: We posted all the activities done in She Leads on social media, and it got a lot of interactions, like comments. Part of it was negative, and the other was positive. We took advantage of the negative part by learning more about how society thinks, so we could improve our way of delivering the message. DCI-Lebanon also strengthened its L&A capacity on WRGE and conducted capacity-building activities around updating its Child Safeguarding and Child Protection policies. The updated policies were rolled out among the team members, employees, volunteers, stakeholders and beneficiaries.
DCI-Lebanon will continue to enhance its organizational capacity, while improving program implementation, and elevating reporting and learning mechanisms for She Leads staff members.

comment.narrative: For 2022, Dar al Amal plans to undertake action to keep the number of girls and young women active within its two gyw-led groups stable. DCI-Lebanon plans to hold its elections and hopes more women will be elected in the board.

As part of the, She Leads program Dar al Amal (DAA) Established 2 GYW-led groups. Each core group in DAA chose a different cause, and they chose it based on the need of their society. For example, in Sabra, which is a Palestinian camp and one the poorest areas in Lebanon, where the GBV cases are high, and children don’t have proper education, the group that we have there chose “custody” to advocate about because a good number of girls in the group are facing this issue and this also reflects the need of their society. But in Nabaa, it’s a different situation, we are still talking about a vulnerable area, but it has lower GBV cases, and children can reach better education, so they chose the topic of environment, which reflects this need of their society. However, due to the economic crisis in Lebanon, some girls and young women need to leave the group and start working. Each core group in DAA chose a different cause, and they chose it based on the need of their society. For example, in Sabra, which is a Palestinian camp and one the poorest areas in Lebanon, where the GBV cases are high, and children don’t have proper education, the group that we have there chose “custody” to advocate about because a good number of girls in the group are facing this issue and this also reflects the need of their society. But in Nabaa, it’s a different situation, we are still talking about a vulnerable area, but it has lower GBV cases, and children can reach better education, so they chose the topic of environment, which reflects this need of their society. Besides, some girls involved got problems with their parents because they were worried about their girls and what they were involved in. DAA wants to keep the number of girls and young women stable, and as such, it organised a meeting with the GYW and their parents, in which they explained what the She Leads programme is about and what is expected from the GYW. This raised the acceptance level among parents to have their girls involved in the She Leads program.Our partner, DCI-Lebanon, elected a new board in February 2022. One-third of the new board is female, which significantly enhances the representation of women within the organisation.
Recruitment of GYW as a staff in DCI: In September 2023, Nour, formerly a GYW group member/ She Leads activist, started in a role of programme coordiantor of She Leads for DCI Lebanon.
